question.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x-6=3t,\,y-3=\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =\frac{x-6}{3},\,{t}^{2}=\frac{2(y-3)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(\frac{x-6}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(x-6)^{2}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=\frac{2(y-3)}{3}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-6)^{2}}{9} & =\frac{2(y-3)}{3} \\ (x-6)^{2} & =9\cdot (\frac{2(y-3)}{3}) \\ (x-6)^{2} & =6(y-3).\end{aligned}
$$
